memories.name: Action Feature System Implementation

Dash ability: spends action, grants extra movement
Dodge ability: spends action, applies DodgingCondition
Disengage ability: spends action, applies DisengagingCondition
Strike action: consumes attack, fires AttackChain
Move action: consumes movement, fires MovementChain
FlurryStrike action: consumes flurry, unarmed attack
OffHandStrike action: consumes off-hand, light weapon
GetSpeed() and GetExtraAttacksCount() (PR #567)
Turn end cleanup: Character.Cleanup() removes temporary actions (PR #568)
All conditions: Raging, Dodging, Disengaging, UnarmoredDefense, SneakAttack, BrutalCritical, MartialArts, UnarmoredMovement, ImprovedCritical, Fighting Styles (6)
ResolveAttack fully implemented in combat/attack.go
Movement integration tests (PR #570 merged)
Proto definitions for action economy (rpg-api-protos #127 merged, v0.1.80)
TurnManager: high-level turn orchestration (PR #573 merged, issue #571 closed)

TurnManager.Strike/Move/OffHandStrike/FlurryStrike - action execution

memories.title: Closed PR #403 - fresh start with toolkit-first approach
memories.context: PR #403 had architectural violations: proto types in orchestrator, business logic that belongs in toolkit, fallback behavior masking issues.
options: Close and start fresh with toolkit-first
memories.chosen: Close and start fresh with toolkit-first
memories.reasoning: PR had 650+ lines of orchestrator code, much of which was game logic. Easier to do it right from scratch than refactor. Toolkit should own Activate/Execute logic, API just orchestrates.
consequences: Need to add combatabilities.Activate() function to toolkit
Need to add actions.Execute() function to toolkit
API orchestrator will be thin - load data, call toolkit, persist
Handler is only place proto types exist

memories.title: TurnManager as high-level turn orchestrator
memories.context: API needs simple entry points for turn actions. Don't want game logic scattered in API.
options: Single TurnManager that owns the turn
memories.chosen: Single TurnManager that owns the turn
memories.reasoning: TurnManager holds all state for a turn: character, economy, room, combatants. Provides clean API: UseAbility, Strike, Move, etc. API just creates TurnManager and calls methods.
consequences: API creates TurnManager per turn with all dependencies
TurnManager owns ActionEconomy, builds context per-call
GetAvailableAbilities/GetAvailableActions for UI queries
StartTurn/EndTurn for lifecycle events

memories.title: Two-level action economy architecture
memories.context: D&D 5e has complex action interactions. Needed a clean separation between spending economy and doing work.
options: Two-level: abilities grant capacity, actions consume it
memories.chosen: Two-level: abilities grant capacity, actions consume it
memories.reasoning: Clean separation of concerns. Abilities are the resource gate, actions are the execution. Makes features and conditions orthogonal.
consequences: Abilities and actions are separate types
Features activate independently
Conditions subscribe to chains, not actions

memories.title: Include available actions in every combat response
memories.context: Toolkit has GetAvailableAbilities/Actions with CanUse and Reason fields. Web needs to know what actions are available after activating abilities (e.g., Flurry of Blows grants FLURRY_STRIKE). Currently would have to derive from ActionEconomy fields.
options: Let web derive from ActionEconomy state
memories.reasoning: Every combat action changes what's available next. Including in response means web just renders what it's told - no duplicate derivation logic. No extra round-trips.
consequences: Need proto messages for AvailableAbility and AvailableAction
ActivateCombatAbilityResponse gains available_actions field
ExecuteActionResponse gains available_actions field
Web becomes simpler - just renders the list

memories.title: Modifier chains for staged pipelines
memories.context: Multiple sources modify attacks and damage (features, conditions, equipment). Need deterministic ordering.
memories.reasoning: base -> features -> conditions -> equipment -> final gives deterministic order. Each stage can see what came before.
consequences: AttackChain and DamageChain are first-class types
Conditions register at specific chain stages
Order is always predictable

memories.title: Conditions as passive bus listeners
memories.context: Conditions like Rage modify damage, Dodge imposes disadvantage. They need to affect combat without being explicitly called.
options: Explicit condition checks in combat code
Conditions subscribe to event bus and modify chains
memories.chosen: Conditions subscribe to event bus and modify chains
memories.reasoning: Keeps combat code clean. Adding a new condition never requires changing existing combat logic. Conditions are self-contained.
consequences: Conditions call Apply(bus) to subscribe
New conditions are additive, not invasive
Testing requires bus setup
